title: Placement from inverse maps
statement: For natural numbers $k,l$, let $f$ map the $k$ positions to the $l$ positions and let $s$ assign to each of the $l$ positions either no position or one of the $k$ positions. Suppose $s(f(i))=i$ for every position $i$, and whenever $s(j)=i$, one has $f(i)=j$. These maps define a placement whose embedding is $f$ and whose selector is $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A map from the $k$ positions to the $l$ positions
A selector from the $l$ positions to either no position or one of the $k$ positions
The selector sends each image $f(i)$ back to $i$
If the selector sends $j$ to $i$, then $f(i)=j$
